ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a cubic die, and the three visible adjacent faces are respectively marked 18, 35, 14, among which 18 is on the upper visible face, 35 is on the left visible face, and 14 is on the right visible face. The problem states that the sum of the numbers on each pair of opposite faces is the same, and that the numbers on all hidden faces are prime numbers. Then reason: Let the common sum of each pair of opposite faces be S. Then the hidden face numbers opposite to 18, 35, 14 are respectively S-18, S-35, S-14, and these three numbers all must be prime numbers. Because S-35 is a prime number, let S-35=q, where q is a prime number, so S=35+q. Thus the other two hidden face numbers are S-18=q+17, S-14=q+21. If q is an odd prime number, then q+17 and q+21 are both even numbers greater than 2, and cannot both be prime numbers. Therefore q can only be 2. Thus S=35+2=37. The number opposite to 14 is S-14=37-14=23.

method.method_draft: Read the cube image: the three visible adjacent faces are labeled 18, 35, and 14. From the text, each opposite pair has the same sum and all hidden opposite-face numbers are prime. Let the common opposite-pair sum be S. Then the hidden numbers are S-18, S-35, and S-14, all prime. Since S-35 is prime, write S=35+q where q is prime. Then the other two hidden numbers are q+17 and q+21. If q were an odd prime, both q+17 and q+21 would be even numbers greater than 2, so they could not be prime. Therefore q=2, giving S=37. The number opposite 14 is S-14=23.

method.method_draft: Read the image first: the visible faces adjacent at the corner show 35, 18, and 14. Let A be the hidden prime opposite 35, B the hidden prime opposite 18, and C the hidden prime opposite 14. The text says all opposite pairs have the same sum, so 35+A=18+B=14+C. Compare each equation to the pair with 35: from 35+A=18+B, get B=A+17; from 35+A=14+C, get C=A+21. Thus the two other hidden primes are 17 and 21 more than the prime opposite 35. If A were an odd prime, then B and C would be even numbers greater than 2, impossible for primes. Hence A must be the only even prime, 2. Then C=2+21=23, so 23 is opposite 14.
